# The last step, and the first moment anything becomes public. Attaches the
# evidence bundle to the draft release and publishes it.
#
# Runs no caller code, which is the whole reason it is a separate job: the
# canon's "attestation happens last, and only on proof" is enforceable only
# while the job that publishes cannot be reached from a build step.
#
# The bundle shape is dictated by what the scoring checks actually match,
# read from Scorecard's source rather than its documentation:
#
#   <name>.spdx.json   Scorecard's SBOM check matches
#                      `.+\.(cdx.json|…|spdx.json|…)`, and awards the full
#                      10 only for an SBOM that is a RELEASE ASSET — 5 if
#                      it exists solely in the repo or the pipeline. Only
#                      the five most recent releases are examined, so this
#                      is a standing obligation, not a one-off.
#   <artifact>.intoto.jsonl
#                      Signed-Releases awards 8 for a signature and 10 only
#                      when provenance is present; `*.intoto.jsonl` is one
#                      of the recognised patterns, and it is also the
#                      filename SLSA's distributing-provenance SHOULD asks
#                      for. One convention satisfies both.
#   checksums.txt      so a consumer can check bytes without tooling.
---
name: attach-release

"on":
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      version:
        # forwarding: universal
        description: Version being released, without the leading v.
        required: true
        type: string
      classes:
        # forwarding: universal
        description: >
          Comma-separated evidence classes this release ships. The
          evidence manifest declares them, and the manifest is written
          here because here is where every asset exists.
        required: true
        type: string
      # The per-LEG split of the build subjects, which only the
      # publisher holds. `stele emit manifest` requires every build
      # subject in `--assets` to be claimed by exactly one build leg —
      # one class and one target (stele#223, manifest schema 4;
      # stele#185 asked the same of the class alone) — and the fan-in
      # below flattens `release-*` with
      # `merge-multiple: true` — so by the time the assets exist here
      # the artifact name that carried the class is gone.
      #
      # The split arrives as inputs rather than being re-derived from
      # un-merged artifact directory names, for three measured reasons.
      # The class of a subject is the BUILD LEG's fact and the
      # orchestrator already holds the leg-to-class map — its attach
      # `if:` names both halves of every pair — so inputs put the fact
      # where the mapping already lives instead of starting a second
      # artifact-name-to-class map here. Each leg computes this string
      # from the same digests, in the same step, that its flat
      # `subjects` output carries — the string that leg's signer signs —
      # so the manifest's typing and the provenance's subject set are
      # derived from ONE source rather than two that must agree. And
      # deriving class from a directory name would rest on
      # download-artifact's layout, which this file already records as
      # inconsistent below: with exactly one artifact matched the
      # download arrives FLAT and the name is gone.
      #
      # Each value is that class's ordinary sha256sum manifest with ONE
      # column added in front: the target whose matrix leg produced the
      # line. The target is likewise a fact of the leg and of nobody
      # else — what a target IS (a platform triple, a runtime major, a
      # publisher's name for a class that varies nothing) is declared
      # by the build workflow that varies it, never inferred here from
      # an asset filename. A class whose matrix runs several legs
      # therefore arrives as one string that the step below splits back
      # into one flag per target; this workflow no longer concatenates
      # anything.
      #
      # oci-image and wasm-npm have no input HERE: those classes publish
      # to a registry and attach no release asset, so they own no build
      # subject and passing their build outputs as one REFUSES. What
      # they published is stated below, as registry subjects.
      #
      # Empty is the ordinary value for a class this release did not
      # build — a skipped job's output is the empty string, and the
      # manifest step writes no flag for an empty one.
      rust-crate-leg-subjects:
        # forwarding: universal
        description: >
          Target-prefixed sha256sum manifest of the crates the
          rust-crate class built, one line per crate.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      rust-binary-leg-subjects:
        # forwarding: universal
        description: >
          Target-prefixed sha256sum manifest of the archives the
          rust-binary class built, one line per archive.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      go-binary-leg-subjects:
        # forwarding: universal
        description: >
          Target-prefixed sha256sum manifest of the archives the
          go-binary class built, one line per archive.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      source-archive-leg-subjects:
        # forwarding: universal
        description: >
          Target-prefixed sha256sum manifest of the archive the
          source-archive class built.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      pgrx-extension-leg-subjects:
        # forwarding: universal
        description: >
          Target-prefixed sha256sum manifest of the tarballs the
          pgrx-extension class built, one line per tarball.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      # What a class published to a REGISTRY instead of beside the
      # release (#1168). An image or a registry package has no file in
      # dist/, so no asset list and no checksum manifest can name it —
      # and a manifest that listed only assets left an image-only
      # release naming no artifact at all, while a mixed one had its
      # registry half skipped by the deep audit in silence. These are
      # where the release says what it shipped there; `stele emit
      # manifest` writes each as a `registry-subject` entry (manifest
      # schema 5), and the audit reads them.
      #
      # Same shape as the leg subjects above and for the same reason:
      # one target-prefixed sha256sum line per subject, computed by the
      # leg from the digests its signer signs. The name is the one the
      # provenance attests — an image reference, a tarball name — never
      # a filename this job could look for.
      #
      # Empty is the ordinary value twice over: for a class this
      # release did not build, and for a rehearsal, which publishes to
      # no registry and must not claim it did.
      oci-image-registry-subjects:
        # forwarding: universal
        description: >
          Target-prefixed sha256sum line of the image index the
          oci-image class published: `image <hex>  <image>`.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      oci-image-class:
        # forwarding: universal
        description: >
          The class that built the image, as the evidence declares it.
          The guard derives it (#843) and it is spelled nowhere else, so
          it arrives rather than being matched out of `classes` here.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: oci-image
      wasm-npm-registry-subjects:
        # forwarding: universal
        description: >
          Target-prefixed sha256sum line of the tarball the wasm-npm
          class published to the npm registry.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      pgrx-extension-image-registry-subjects:
        # forwarding: universal
        description: >
          Target-prefixed sha256sum manifest of the per-major image
          indexes a pgrx release published, one line per major.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      pgrx-extension-image-class:
        # forwarding: universal
        description: >
          The class those images are attributed to, as the evidence
          declares it. Derived by the guard beside the image class and
          spelled nowhere else; empty when no extension was declared,
          which is also when there are no images to attribute.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      dry-run:
        # forwarding: universal
        description: Rehearsal — attach the bundle, leave the release a draft.
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
    secrets:
      app-private-key:
        # forwarding: universal
        description: Tag-mint App private key
        required: true

permissions: {}

jobs:
  attach:
    name: Attach the evidence bundle and publish
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions: {}
    env:
      MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS: ${{ github.workspace }}
      MISE_LOCKED: "1"
      MISE_GLOBAL_CONFIG_FILE: ${{ github.workspace }}/.org-canon/mise/config.toml
    steps:
      # The checkout comes FIRST and cannot move: actions/checkout cleans
      # the workspace, so a checkout placed after the downloads deletes
      # the very dist/ this job assembled. Measured on v1.45.1, whose
      # attach died on `cd: dist: No such file or directory`.
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Resolve the canon tree (the ref the caller pinned)
        uses: $/.github/actions/canon

      - name: Install mise and the pinned toolchain
        uses: jdx/mise-action@b44d12e7d0d8ee7461bb893e1b1993500433185b # v5.2.7
        with:
          version: 2026.11.4
          cache: false

      # By pattern, not by name: every build class uploads its assets as
      # `release-*` and every sign job its bundle as `attestation-bundle-*`,
      # so any subset of classes fans in here without this step knowing
      # which. A class that pushed only to a registry (oci-image)
      # contributes a bundle and no files, which is why an empty dist is
      # legal below while an empty bundle set is not.
      #
      # The merge is what erases class from the assets, and the manifest
      # needs class back — which is what the per-class subjects inputs
      # above carry. The BYTES still arrive here and only here; the
      # inputs say which class each of them belongs to, and nothing is
      # trusted from them but that split.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: release-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: dist

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: attestation-bundle-*
          path: bundle

      - name: Name each provenance after the class it describes
        env:
          DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry-run }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # SLSA distributing-provenance: provenance "SHOULD have a
          # filename that is directly related to the build artifact
          # filename". One bundle covers one class's subjects, so each is
          # named for its class — attestations-<class>.intoto.jsonl, still
          # inside the `*.intoto.jsonl` pattern Scorecard's Signed-Releases
          # check recognises.
          mkdir -p dist
          found=0
          for dir in bundle/attestation-bundle-*/; do
            [[ -d ${dir} ]] || continue
            class=$(basename "${dir}")
            class="${class#attestation-bundle-}"
            # -print -quit, never `| head -1`: find's own first-match stop, so
            # there is no pipe to break and no walk to finish (#682).
            src=$(find "${dir}" -type f -print -quit)
            [[ -n ${src} ]] || {
              echo "::error::empty bundle for ${class}"
              exit 1
            }
            mv "${src}" "dist/attestations-${class}.intoto.jsonl"
            found=$((found + 1))
          done
          if ((found == 0)); then
            # download-artifact is layout-inconsistent, measured across two
            # releases: two matched artifacts arrive in per-name
            # subdirectories, exactly one arrives FLAT in the target path.
            # The flat case carries no artifact name, so the class cannot
            # be recovered — and with a single bundle it need not be: one
            # bundle covering the whole release truthfully takes the
            # umbrella name, which is the same `*.intoto.jsonl` pattern
            # Scorecard recognises and SLSA's naming SHOULD asks for.
            # -print -quit, never `| head -1`: find's own first-match stop, so
            # there is no pipe to break and no walk to finish (#682).
            flat=$(find bundle -maxdepth 1 -type f -print -quit 2> /dev/null)
            if [[ -n ${flat} ]]; then
              mv "${flat}" "dist/attestations.intoto.jsonl"
              found=1
            fi
          fi
          if ((found == 0)); then
            if [[ ${DRY_RUN} == "true" ]]; then
              # An oci-only rehearsal signs nothing: its signer runs only
              # against a really-pushed digest. Loud, never silent.
              echo "::warning::rehearsal: no Sigstore bundle to attach"
            else
              echo "::error::no Sigstore bundle — a release without evidence does not publish"
              exit 1
            fi
          fi
          echo "::notice::${found} attestation bundle(s) attached"
      - name: Assert the SBOM arrived
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Generation moved to the publish orchestrator's sbom job (and,
          # for images, the build's pull-back step) — class-shaped, derived
          # from what actually ships (docs/dependency-track.md). This job
          # runs no tooling, so it only asserts the inventory is present:
          # a release without one blinds audit:blast-radius and caps
          # Scorecard's SBOM check, silently.
          #
          # -name over a glob: the dist/* glob skips dotfiles, which is
          # how every canon release (.github -> .github-x.y.z.spdx.json)
          # shipped SBOM-less with everything green. Names are dot-proofed
          # at generation now; this assertion is the backstop.
          n=$(find dist -maxdepth 1 -name "*.spdx.json" | wc -l | tr -d " ")
          if [[ ${n} -eq 0 ]]; then
            echo "::error::no SBOM in dist — the sbom job should have delivered one"
            exit 1
          fi
          hidden=$(find dist -maxdepth 1 -name ".*" -type f | wc -l | tr -d " ")
          if [[ ${hidden} -ne 0 ]]; then
            echo "::error::dotfile in dist — dist/* globs and the checksum loop would silently skip it"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "::notice::${n} SBOM(s) in the bundle"
      # The declared contract, attested at the tag (stele#40, from
      # #109): which classes shipped, the verdict layout, the machinery
      # version obligations are derived from, and every asset pinned and
      # TYPED as a build subject or an evidence document — written by
      # `stele emit manifest` through the same definition the assert
      # reader decodes, and proven readable on its own rendered bytes
      # before anything ships it.
      #
      # It is written HERE, in the fan-in, because here is the first
      # moment the release's assets all exist. Written in the sbom job
      # it saw only the inventory that job had just derived, and typed
      # one entry where the release published five — the build subject
      # among them, so the repro walk's population was empty and its
      # verdict CANNOT_JUDGE. Measured on v1.45.0.
      - name: Write the evidence manifest
        env:
          CLASSES: ${{ inputs.classes }}
          SUBJECTS_RUST_CRATE: ${{ inputs.rust-crate-leg-subjects }}
          SUBJECTS_RUST_BINARY: ${{ inputs.rust-binary-leg-subjects }}
          SUBJECTS_GO_BINARY: ${{ inputs.go-binary-leg-subjects }}
          SUBJECTS_SOURCE_ARCHIVE: ${{ inputs.source-archive-leg-subjects }}
          SUBJECTS_PGRX_EXTENSION: ${{ inputs.pgrx-extension-leg-subjects }}
          REGISTRY_OCI_IMAGE: ${{ inputs.oci-image-registry-subjects }}
          OCI_IMAGE_CLASS: ${{ inputs.oci-image-class }}
          REGISTRY_WASM_NPM: ${{ inputs.wasm-npm-registry-subjects }}
          REGISTRY_PGRX_EXTENSION_IMAGE: ${{ inputs.pgrx-extension-image-registry-subjects }}
          PGRX_EXTENSION_IMAGE_CLASS: ${{ inputs.pgrx-extension-image-class }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The machinery version is the canon tree's own, read from the
          # version mirror the pinned tree carries — the caller's `uses:`
          # ref is a commit SHA (the tag-pin rule), so the version is a
          # fact about the TREE, not about the ref's spelling. For the
          # canon's own releases the mirror already carries the version
          # being cut, so one read covers both cases.
          machinery=$(awk '/^version:/{print $2; exit}' .org-canon/CITATION.cff)
          [[ -n ${machinery} ]] || {
            echo "::error::the pinned canon tree's CITATION.cff names no version — the manifest cannot state its machinery"
            exit 1
          }
          # Pass one of two: everything the release ships BEFORE the
          # manifest exists, because a manifest cannot pin itself and
          # the format says so. The checksum step below is pass two and
          # covers everything including it.
          (cd dist && sha256sum ./* | sed 's| \./| |') > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/assets.sha256"
          # The leg split, one --leg-subjects per (class, target) that
          # built something. stele demands every build subject in
          # --assets be claimed by exactly one leg, so a class whose
          # matrix ran contributes one flag per target it built and a
          # class that did not run contributes nothing. An unset input
          # is the empty string, so this loop is also what makes a
          # single-class release pass exactly the flags its one class
          # earned.
          # Named once each, class beside its input: no name mangling
          # between the two, so a class that is added or renamed is one
          # line here and grep finds it.
          #
          # The target column is READ, never invented: the leg that
          # built the artifact wrote it. A line without one refuses
          # rather than defaulting, because a build subject with no
          # target goes unjudged by every scoped rebuild — silently,
          # which is the failure #637 exists to end.
          #
          # The registry subjects ride the same function under their own
          # flag: the grammar is one, and what differs is only which
          # population stele places the line in. The flag is part of the
          # file name so a class that one day has both cannot have one
          # leg's file overwrite the other's.
          #
          # A class NAME that arrives empty beside subjects that do not
          # is the orchestrator contradicting itself, and is refused
          # here rather than handed to stele as a leg with no class.
          subject_flags=()
          claim() {
            local flag="$1" class="$2" legs="$3" line target path
            local -a targets=()
            [[ -n ${legs//[[:space:]]/} ]] || return 0
            if [[ -z ${class} ]]; then
              echo "::error::${flag}: subjects arrived with no class to attribute them to"
              exit 1
            fi
            while IFS= read -r line; do
              [[ -n ${line//[[:space:]]/} ]] || continue
              target="${line%% *}"
              line="${line#* }"
              if [[ -z ${target} || ${line} == "${target}" ]]; then
                echo "::error::${class}: subject line names no target — an untargeted artifact no scoped rebuild judges"
                exit 1
              fi
              if [[ ${target} =~ [^A-Za-z0-9._-] ]]; then
                echo "::error::${class}: target ${target} is not a plain name — it becomes a file this step writes"
                exit 1
              fi
              path="${RUNNER_TEMP}/${flag}-${class}-${target}.sha256"
              if [[ " ${targets[*]-} " != *" ${target} "* ]]; then
                targets+=("${target}")
                : > "${path}"
                subject_flags+=("--${flag}" "${class}:${target}=${path}")
              fi
              printf '%s\n' "${line}" >> "${path}"
            done <<< "${legs}"
            echo "::notice::${class} claims ${#targets[@]} ${flag} leg(s): ${targets[*]}"
          }
          claim leg-subjects rust-crate "${SUBJECTS_RUST_CRATE}"
          claim leg-subjects rust-binary "${SUBJECTS_RUST_BINARY}"
          claim leg-subjects go-binary "${SUBJECTS_GO_BINARY}"
          claim leg-subjects source-archive "${SUBJECTS_SOURCE_ARCHIVE}"
          claim leg-subjects pgrx-extension "${SUBJECTS_PGRX_EXTENSION}"
          claim registry-subjects "${OCI_IMAGE_CLASS}" "${REGISTRY_OCI_IMAGE}"
          claim registry-subjects wasm-npm "${REGISTRY_WASM_NPM}"
          claim registry-subjects "${PGRX_EXTENSION_IMAGE_CLASS}" "${REGISTRY_PGRX_EXTENSION_IMAGE}"
          stele emit manifest \
            --classes "${CLASSES}" \
            --store-vsa true \
            --machinery-version "${machinery}" \
            --assets "${RUNNER_TEMP}/assets.sha256" \
            "${subject_flags[@]}" \
            --assert-policy .org-canon/slsa/assert-policy.json \
            --out dist/evidence-manifest.json
      - name: Checksum everything that ships
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cd dist
          # Never written into the directory it hashes (#1196): the
          # redirect belongs to sed, both halves start together, and a
          # checksums.txt created before the glob expands was listed at
          # the empty-file digest (release-lab v0.28.1).
          [[ ! -e checksums.txt ]] || {
            echo "::error::dist/checksums.txt exists before it is written"
            exit 1
          }
          sha256sum ./* | sed 's| \./| |' > "${RUNNER_TEMP}/checksums.txt"
          mv "${RUNNER_TEMP}/checksums.txt" checksums.txt
      - name: Mint the publishing token
        id: token
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        with:
          client-id: ${{ vars.TAG_MINT_APP_CLIENT_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.app-private-key }}
          permission-contents: write

      - name: Attach and publish
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.token.outputs.token }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry-run }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Post-publish resume converges, never clobbers (#316, found on
          # v1.20.0's first mint): the DOI job runs AFTER publish, so a
          # mint-only failure (the issuer down) is re-dispatched into a
          # release that is already published and immutable — where
          # --clobber's delete is refused with a 422 and the resume dies
          # before reaching the one job that actually failed. If the
          # release is out, prove the rebuilt bytes equal the published
          # bytes and pass through; a mismatch is a real failure, not a
          # resume.
          draft=$(gh release view "${TAG}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft)
          if [[ ${draft} == "false" ]]; then
            gh release download "${TAG}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
              --pattern checksums.txt --output published-checksums.txt
            # What must be identical is the BUILD SUBJECTS, and which
            # assets those are is the published manifest's own typing to
            # say (stele#156) — not this step's guess. Comparing the
            # whole manifest made a resume impossible whenever an
            # evidence document legitimately differed: a Sigstore
            # signature embeds a fresh timestamp and certificate on
            # every signing, so a re-signed bundle changes bytes by
            # design, and an SBOM exported live from the forge's
            # dependency graph can too. Measured on v1.44.1's duplicate
            # tag push, where the resume could never converge.
            gh release download "${TAG}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
              --pattern evidence-manifest.json --output published-manifest.json 2> /dev/null || true
            subjects=""
            if [[ -s published-manifest.json ]]; then
              subjects=$(jq -r '(.entries // [])[] | select(.type == "build-subject") | .name' \
                published-manifest.json)
            fi
            if [[ -z ${subjects} ]]; then
              # A release published before entries were typed (schema 1
              # carries no `entries`) has no answer to give, so the
              # whole-set comparison stands for it. Pre-epoch releases
              # keep the guard they shipped under; nothing is rewritten
              # to make them look newer than they are.
              if ! diff -u published-checksums.txt dist/checksums.txt; then
                emsg="${TAG} is published and immutable but the rebuilt assets differ from the published set — this is"
                emsg+=" not a resume"
                echo "::error::${emsg}"
                exit 1
              fi
            else
              differing=""
              while IFS= read -r name; do
                [[ -n ${name} ]] || continue
                was=$(awk -v n="${name}" '$2 == n {print $1}' published-checksums.txt)
                now=$(awk -v n="${name}" '$2 == n {print $1}' dist/checksums.txt)
                if [[ -z ${was} || -z ${now} || ${was} != "${now}" ]]; then
                  differing="${differing} ${name}"
                fi
              done <<< "${subjects}"
              if [[ -n ${differing} ]]; then
                emsg="${TAG} is published and immutable but these build subjects differ from the published bytes:"
                emsg+="${differing} — this is not a resume"
                echo "::error::${emsg}"
                exit 1
              fi
            fi
            echo "::notice::${TAG} already published; build subjects verified identical, converging"
            exit 0
          fi
          gh release upload "${TAG}" dist/* --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          if [[ ${DRY_RUN} == "true" ]]; then
            # The draft stays on purpose here — and to anyone reading the
            # releases page that is indistinguishable from a burn, which
            # is how the org accumulated thirty-two drafts nobody could
            # classify by looking (#597). The reason is known HERE and
            # nowhere later, so it is written down here.
            REPO="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" TAG="${TAG}" KIND=rehearsal \
              RUN_URL="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" \
              .org-canon/release/record-draft.sh
            echo "::warning::rehearsal: ${TAG} left as a draft, nothing published"
            exit 0
          fi
          # Publishing is the commitment point. Immutable releases apply at
          # publish, and GitHub mints its own release attestation binding
          # tag, commit and asset digests at the same moment.
          gh release edit "${TAG}" --draft=false --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          echo "::notice::published ${TAG}"
...
